Read this as a warning, not as proof. The IML warehouse file carries no customer name, and I tested every reference we have against it: 391 customer order and reference numbers in the 16 per-distributor walkthroughs, plus the central file - not one matches IML's 140 order numbers. The two number ranges are different systems. So no delayed warehouse line can be attributed to a distributor. What follows is the closest honest statement: a part that is delayed in the warehouse and still open on a distributor's order. It is the same part number, not a traced document.

The parts where a distributor is waiting and the warehouse is holding

Click a row to filter to that part. For a single distributor's parts and waiting times, click that distributor's bar above.

This is the cleanest evidence of a supply weakness. A part that appears on the back-order list in one week may be a single late ship. A part that appears week after week, ordered again and again and never arriving, is not a warehouse that was slow - it is a part that never came. UTI is the only market where we hold a continuous weekly series: 39 lists, week 2 to week 40 of 2026.

Fill rate is the share of an order the distributor gets first time. It is the number most directly downstream of IML shipping speed. The target column is each distributor's own target from the FY26-27 KPI targets, which sit on a network standard of 95% and a floor of 92%. Where a cell says N/D the distributor does not report, so it is named and left empty - no value is invented.

Two vocabularies, side by side

Every table that shows a family now shows AIM family and Catalogue category next to each other. They are two different vocabularies - the AIM family is our aftersales classification, the catalogue category is the parts tree - so they are shown side by side and neither is passed off as the other. Where a line has neither, the AIM column says so and the catalogue column stays blank rather than repeating it.

Why the warehouse reads less than the backlog

A small separate point, worth one line: 163 real AIM family names that once existed in aim_pn_classification.csv.bak_pre_eq_20260917 are empty in the current master. That is a restore item, not a rebuild, and it is not a sign that family coverage was lost at scale - an earlier reading suggesting that was withdrawn after checking, because the old file was mostly the catalogue category sitting in a column named aim_l1, and the catalogue is still held in cat_l1.

What is missing, and what it would unlock

MissingWhat it would answerWho has it

What I checked and did not find

  • Customer order number against IML order number: zero matches.
  • Customer reference against IML order number: zero matches.
  • Part number against the warehouse file: it matches, but a part is not a customer.
  • Dispatch and arrival dates: Invoice, Shipped and ETD are empty on all 2,102 rows, so this file cannot show a voyage at all.
  • PBI will not close it either: Power BI reads the same SAP, and SAP records billing, not shipping.

What everything means

TermMeaning
Order NoThe purchase order IML's warehouse works to. 140 of them in this file.
ProccedThe date IML processed the order. Where the waiting time starts.
Process statusTo be picked, to be packed, ready for shipment, back order. It says where a line is, not whether it is late.
Ready for shipmentPacked and finished, waiting to leave the building.
MoT / ModeSea or air freight.
Days waiting2 October 2026 minus the processed date. This is time inside IML, not time at sea.
AIM familyThe family a part belongs to in our own aftersales classification: Chassis Frame, Brakes, Maintenance Service and so on. Filled in from the parts we bill, so a part we have never sold has none.
Catalogue categoryThe top level of the parts tree. A different vocabulary from the AIM family and much more complete, because it comes from the catalogue rather than from what we have sold. Shown beside the AIM family, never instead of it.
First fill rateShare of an order supplied first time, without a back order.
MOSMonths of stock. Days of parts in stock, against the distributor's own band.
Back-order linesOrder lines the distributor could not get, reported monthly.

Where the numbers come from

IML warehouse: ISZE order status as of 2 October 2026, sheet isze.

Customer backlog: Natalie Vernimmen, backlog info file VP, week 41, 6 October 2026.

Per-distributor week 41 files: 16 separate mail attachments, used only for the reference test that failed.

Recurrence: 39 weekly BO overview lists for UTI, week 2 to week 40 of 2026.

Fill rate and back orders: KPI Master File august 2026, sheet Parts Handling, latest reported month per distributor. Targets: ISZE DB KPI Targets FY26-27, sheet Targets FY26-27.

Scope: VP distributors, MIDI and the Russia and Kazakhstan accounts excluded from the backlog side. No euro valuation on this page.
